summary: Changbaishan Airport (NBS) is a regional gateway in southeastern Jilin Province, China, primarily serving tourists traveling to the Changbai Mountain Nature Reserve and the famous Tianchi (Heaven Lake) crater lake on the China–North Korea border. Opened in 2008, it sits in a forested valley at an elevation of about 900 meters and connects this remote natural attraction to major Chinese cities including Beijing, Shanghai, and Harbin. The airport operates predominantly during the warmer tourist seasons, with reduced schedules in winter due to harsh weather conditions.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines fly to Changbaishan Airport?
A: Major Chinese carriers including China Southern, China Eastern, Air China, and Shanghai Airlines operate seasonal and year-round routes from cities like Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou, with schedules typically peaking in summer.

Q: How far is the airport from Changbai Mountain scenic area?
A: The airport is roughly 130 km from the main Changbai Mountain North Slope entrance and the Tianchi lake area, requiring a 2-2.5 hour drive by road or shuttle bus.

Q: When is the best time to fly into Changbaishan?
A: Summer (June to September) offers the best weather and clearest views of Tianchi Lake, though autumn foliage in late September and October is also spectacular.

Q: Are there international flights from NBS?
A: No, Changbaishan Airport currently handles only domestic Chinese flights.
transport_tips: Pre-booked hotel shuttles and tourist bus services are the most common way to reach the Changbai Mountain scenic area, as public transit options are limited. Taxi service is available at the terminal but fares to the mountain attractions are expensive due to the long distance, so negotiate or arrange return transport in advance. Rental cars are available but driving in winter requires caution due to snow and ice on mountain roads.
local_tip: Pack a light jacket even in summer
